payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Comparing the source and edited images, is the source mug's requested move to the right of the headphones complete, incomplete with visible progress, or not made?
node.criteria: Pass only if visual correspondence establishes that the source mug is positioned to the right of the headphones in the edited image, satisfying the requested move. Fail if the source mug is identifiable and remains at its source-side position with no visible progress toward the right, or if it is identifiable in an intermediate position and the requested final position is not achieved. If the source mug is identifiable and evidence shows it remains at the source location while a plausible corresponding mug has appeared or moved toward the right, treat the move as incomplete rather than complete. Do not count an unrelated mug on the right as completion. Use unknown only when the source mug's correspondence or its position/progress cannot be determined from the images.
node.binding: Compare the source image's light-blue mug—including its body shape, handle, appearance, and original position left of the headphones—with all mug-like objects and any visible remnants in the edited image. Assess the pale mug left of the headphones, the mug right of them, and the blue-looking blurred patch at the far left as possible correspondence evidence; altered color or appearance alone does not rule out identity. Determine whether the source mug is still at its original location, has plausibly moved toward the right, or is visibly to the right of the headphones. Base the decision on source-to-edited visual evidence and the requested move, not on mug count or right-side position alone; retain unknown if correspondence or progress remains genuinely indeterminate.

node_traces.evidence: The source light-blue mug is left of the headphones. In the edited image, a pale mug remains left of the headphones, while a separate mug is to their right; the blue-looking blurred patch at far left also suggests the source mug remains at its original side rather than being moved. The right-side mug therefore does not establish completion of the source mug's move.

response.content: {"text":"The trace correctly rejects completion: the right-side mug alone does not establish that it is the source mug. But its own evidence also describes a blue-looking remnant at the source location and a pale mug still left of the headphones, alongside a newly present right-side mug. That is evidence of some attempted change, not “no requested change,” so the all-or-nothing pass/fail criterion is collapsing visible partial progress into `no` and conflicts with the reference `partial`. Refine the decision node’s outcome mapping to distinguish complete, incomplete-with-visible-progress, and no progress: keep the right-side mug insufficient for completion, but assess whether the source mug’s appearance/location has been altered or a plausible corresponding mug has moved toward the target while remnants remain. Compare source-to-edited correspondence using shape, handle, color, scale, and location; do not treat the blurred blue patch as conclusive proof of either identity or no movement. Use `unknown` only if correspondence/progress is genuinely indeterminate. The trace is valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is a visual-criterion/calibration issue, not a transport or schema failure; its 0.91 confidence merits review given the ambiguous remnants."}
